title: Needle Python Docs
summary: The reference for the cactus-compute package: the Cactus class, tools three ways, the response shape, the behaviour contract, system facts, speech, vision, tuned weights, offline devices, environments, the CLI, and the mistakes to avoid.
body_markdown:
` cactus-compute` is inference, LoRA fine-tuning and export for Needle 3 in one Python package. Text goes in, a JSON tool call comes back; a byte-level grammar compiled from your schemas constrains every token, so the call is always well-formed. A sub-1 MB engine and the` needle3.cact` weights are fetched once from Hugging Face and cached; nothing is compiled locally. This page is the reference. The guides on[designing tools](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/designing-tools-for-needle) ,[confidence](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/needle-confidence) ,[extraction](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/structured-extraction-with-needle) ,[fine-tuning](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/finetuning-needle) and[devices](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/needle-supported-devices) are the narrative.


## Install


```text
pip   install   -U   cactus-compute               # runtime, text, speech and vision
pip   install   "cactus-compute[mic]"           # adds microphone capture and resampling
pip   install   "cactus-compute[train]"         # adds JAX and the training deps
pip   install   "cactus-compute[train,gpu]"     # NVIDIA
pip   install   "cactus-compute[train,metal]"   # Apple Silicon
```


` import cactus` is lightweight and never imports JAX; only` cactus finetune` and` cactus build` do. The engine downloads on the first` Cactus(...)` . Anonymous usage counts (function name, package version, OS, a random install id; never prompts, outputs or data) can be switched off with` CACTUS_TELEMETRY=0` or` DO_NOT_TRACK=1` , and CI environments are excluded automatically.


## API


Call What it does


` cactus.Cactus(tools=None, system=None, weights=None, tool_index_path=None, buffer_size=65536, auto_date=True, generation=3)` An agent bound to one toolset.` tools` takes decorated functions, Pydantic models, raw JSON-schema dicts or a JSON string.` system` carries environment facts.` weights` loads a tuned` .cact` .` tool_index_path` is reserved for engine index archives. Cactus 4 runs Needle 3.


` agent.run(query, max_steps=8, max_new_tokens=512, strict=True)` The full loop: the model picks calls, Needle executes your functions and feeds results back, and the final response carries the executed tool results as` results` .


` agent.complete(text="", max_new_tokens=512, *, audio=None, language=None, keywords=None, word_timestamps=False)` One turn. You execute the call and feed the result back through the next` complete(...)` .


` agent.embed(text)` A normalized vector for text, from the embedding head or the confidence probe pool.


` agent.reset()` Rewind the conversation, keep the tools loaded.


` cactus.tool` Decorator that turns a function into a tool schema.` @cactus.tool(triggers=\[...\])` adds request regexes.


` cactus.Field(...)` Per-argument constraints, attached inline with` typing.Annotated` or passed as a default.


` cactus.extract(text, schema, system=None, max_new_tokens=512, weights=None, strict=True, generation=None)` One-shot extraction. A Pydantic instance if` schema` is a model, else a dict, or` None` if nothing matched.` weights` loads a tuned` .cact` ; without it the base Needle 3 model runs.` strict=True` raises` cactus.ExtractionValidationError` instead of returning a date whose year contradicts the text or a value the engine flags as invented or negated.


` cactus.transcribe(audio, language=None, keywords=None, word_timestamps=False, weights=None)`[Whistle](https://www.cactuscompute.com/blog/whistle) , the speech model, on the same engine. A WAV path or 16 kHz mono float samples of any length, one pass up to 30 s and windowed beyond it. Returns` text` ,` language` ,` ttft_ms` and` decode_tps` , plus` words` with start, end and probability when timestamps are on.


` cactus.Whistle(weights=None, buffer_size=262144)` The same model as an object, for` whistle.embed(audio)` , the encoder output at one row per 80 ms frame. Calls are serialized through the shared runtime.


## Speech


```text
import   cactus


print  (cactus.transcribe(  "clip.wav"  )[  "text"  ])
```


` language` is one of` en de fr es it nl pl` , or` None` to detect it.` keywords` takes a list or a newline-separated string and biases the search towards the names your users say. Silence and steady noise return an empty text and an empty language rather than an invented sentence; other sounds, music especially, can still come out as text, so put a voice activity detector or a wake word in front of an always-on microphone. A 16 kHz WAV or raw samples need nothing beyond the base install; other sample rates and the microphone need the` \[mic\]` extra.


The weights are a separate download from the engine, which is shared:` whistle.cact` comes from[Cactus-Compute/whistle](https://huggingface.co/Cactus-Compute/whistle) on first use, and` CACTUS_WHISTLE_WEIGHTS` points at a local copy. In the native engine the two models load side by side and` cactus_complete` takes a clip directly; from Python they are two objects over one library.


## Tools, three ways


The decorator reads the signature for types, the docstring for the description, a Google-style` Args:` block for per-argument descriptions; a default makes an argument optional and a` Literal` becomes a fixed set the model cannot leave:


```text
import   cactus
from   typing   import   Annotated, Literal


@cactus.tool
def   set_thermostat  (temperature:   int  , mode: Literal[  "heat"  ,   "cool"  ,   "auto"  ]   =   "auto"  ):
"""Set the thermostat.


Args:
temperature: target temperature in Celsius
mode: heating strategy to use
"""
return   {  "temperature"  : temperature,   "mode"  : mode}


@cactus.tool  (  triggers  =  [  r  "  \b(  turn  |  switch  |  power  |  flip  )\b.  *  \b(  on  |  off  )\b  "  ,   r  "  \b  toggle  \b  "  ])
def   control_device  (device:   str  , action: Literal[  "on"  ,   "off"  ,   "toggle"  ]):
"Switch or toggle any named smart-home device."
return   {  "device"  : device,   "action"  : action}
```


` cactus.Field` constrains values, and every constraint is compiled into the decode grammar:


```text
@cactus.tool
def   send_money  (
amount: Annotated[  float  , cactus.Field(  gt  =  0  ,   le  =  10000  ,   description  =  "USD, up to 10,000"  )],
to:     Annotated[  str  ,   cactus.Field(  pattern  =  r  "  ^  @  [a-z0-9_]  +  $  "  ,   description  =  "recipient handle"  )],
memo:   Annotated[  str  ,   cactus.Field(  max_length  =  80  )]   =   ""  ,
):
"Send money to a handle."
return   {  "sent"  : amount,   "to"  : to}
```


` Field` takes` description` ,` enum` ,` const` ,` ge` /` le` /` gt` /` lt` ,` multiple_of` ,` min_length` /` max_length` ,` pattern` ,` format` ,` min_items` /` max_items` and` unique_items` . A raw JSON schema is exactly what the engine consumes, and takes the same` "triggers"` list beside` description` :


```text
tools   =   [{
"name"  :   "set_lights"  ,
"description"  :   "Turn a room's lights on or off and set brightness"  ,
"parameters"  : {
"type"  :   "object"  ,
"properties"  : {
"room"  : {  "type"  :   "string"  ,   "description"  :   "which room to control"  },
"on"  : {  "type"  :   "boolean"  },
"brightness"  : {  "type"  :   "integer"  ,   "minimum"  :   0  ,   "maximum"  :   100  },
},
"required"  : [  "room"  ,   "on"  ],
},
}]
agent   =   cactus.Cactus(  tools  =  tools)
```


OpenAI-style` {"type": "function", "function": {...}}` wrappers are accepted too. Java, JavaScript and camel-cased names are converted to collision-safe snake-case aliases for the model and restored exactly in the returned calls; descriptions, enum values and defaults are never rewritten.


## The loop


run() executes each call against your decorated functions, feeds the JSON result back as the next turn, and stops at a respond turn or max_steps. complete() gives you one turn at a time when you want to own execution.


```text
import   json


agent   =   cactus.Cactus(  tools  =  [set_thermostat, control_device])
agent.run(  "make it 21 and cool the room"  )[  "results"  ]


r   =   agent.complete(  "toggle the garage door"  )
if   r[  "type"  ]   ==   "call"  :
out   =   control_device(  **  r[  "function_calls"  ][  0  ][  "arguments"  ])
r   =   agent.complete(json.dumps(out))
```


A turn after a call is a tool result only when it parses as JSON; any other text is a new user turn. Later arguments may depend on earlier results (` search_for_contact` first, then` send_instant_message` with the returned id). A final` "type": "respond"` with empty` function_calls` ends the loop; the answer is the tool results, which` run()` collects as` results` . No free text is generated.


## The response


```text
{
"type"  :   "call"  ,
"success"  :   true  ,
"error"  :   null  ,
"error_code"  :   null  ,
"function_calls"  : [ {   "name"  :   "set_lights"  ,   "arguments"  : {   "room"  :   "living room"  ,   "on"  :   true  ,   "brightness"  :   30   } } ],
"suppressed_calls"  : [],
"reasoning"  :   "'living room' -> room; 'dim' -> on true, brightness 30"  ,
"confidence"  :   0.94  ,
"prefill_tps"  :   4300.0  ,
"decode_tps"  :   850.0  ,
"peak_ram_mb"  :   88.5
}
```


- ` function_calls` is a list of` {"name", "arguments"}` ;` arguments` is grammar-guaranteed to match your schema. Empty is the refusal for off-topic input.
- ` suppressed_calls` holds a call the engine withheld: confidence under 0.1, or a grounding gate. Show it to confirm, or treat the turn as a refusal.
- ` reasoning` is the model's short, unconstrained derivation of each argument from its source span.
- ` confidence` is calibrated for the base model; it is` None` for tuned weights.
- ` validation.ungrounded` , when present, lists` tool.field` names whose value the package could not ground, including a date whose year appears nowhere in the conversation or the` system` facts.` run()` refuses those calls with` {"error": "ungrounded field"}` unless` strict=False` .


## The contract


- A request no declared tool can serve is refused with the empty call` \[\]` . There is no free-text fallback; always handle the empty case.
- Arguments contain only values evidenced by the input. An optional field with no evidence is omitted, not guessed; do not assume a key exists.
- Arguments arrive after the engine's deterministic repair, grounded in the request: split names, completed phone numbers, verbatim quotes, recovered place queries, weekday and` March 4th` dates against the` date:` fact, polarity from the request verb, enums moved to the option the request names, routes from` from X to Y` ,` by N` into a lone number argument, invented required slots refilled from the request or the schema default, ungrounded optional values dropped, and calls the request excludes or negates dropped.
- One toolset per agent. Later turns are bare queries against the same tools;` reset()` rewinds the conversation. New tools mean a new` Cactus(...)` .
- ` Cactus(system=...)` prefixes the local` date:` fact automatically unless the text already carries one;` auto_date=False` opts out.


## System facts


```text
agent   =   cactus.Cactus(  tools  =  tools,   system  =  "date: 2026-07-21 Tue 14:30; locale: en-US; device: phone; battery: 62%"  )
```


Recognised keys:` date` ,` locale` ,` device` ,` battery` ,` network` ,` location` ,` user` ,` assistant` . Facts, never instructions: the model resolves relative language against them and is not steered by prose placed there. Omitting the turn is safe.


## Toolsets and custom weights


Needle 3 reads the complete toolset in its prompt. Keep tool names plain and toolsets small. It has no retrieval head.


` weights="tuned.cact"` loads an archive from` cactus build` . Each tuned text agent runs in its own worker process with its own model and conversation. Base and tuned agents can run together. Cactus 4 supports Needle 3, Whistle and Mirage. Needle 2 remains available through` cactus-compute<4` and the GitHub repository's` legacy` branch.


## Speech and vision


` cactus.Whistle()` transcribes WAV files or 16 kHz mono float samples. Use` agent.complete(audio="clip.wav", language="en")` for an audio tool call. Its result combines the tool-call envelope with` audio_text` and the speech metrics. Supply text or audio in each call.


` cactus.Mirage()` accepts file paths, encoded image bytes, Pillow images or RGB uint8 arrays. Packed RGB bytes require explicit` width` and` height` .


```text
import   cactus


vision   =   cactus.Mirage()
result   =   vision.describe(  "photo.png"  ,   sections  =  [  "objects"  ,   "text"  ],   fields  =  [  "bbox"  ,   "mask"  ])
form   =   vision.extract(  "photo.png"  , {  "animal"  : {  "enum"  : [  "dog"  ,   "cat"  ]}})
```


` describe` accepts` language` ,` keywords` and the native vision options, including confidence thresholds, object limits, output sections and mask format.` extract` accepts ordered fields with` enum` , bounded` integer` ,` string` and box references. Text, speech and vision share one engine and calls are serialized across threads.


## Offline devices


The engine comes from[Cactus-Compute/cactus](https://huggingface.co/Cactus-Compute/cactus) , with a pinned commit and SHA-256 checksums. Weights have independent pins in the Needle 3, Whistle and Mirage repositories. Engine files are cached under` ~/.cache/cactus/engine/<version>/<commit>/` and models under` ~/.cache/cactus/models/<model>/<commit>/` .` XDG_CACHE_HOME` can relocate the cache.


1. Run` cactus fetch` on a connected machine to download the engine.` --platform-tag manylinux2014_aarch64` selects another runtime. Run` cactus download needle3` ,` cactus download whistle` or` cactus download mirage` for the weights.
2. Copy the cache to the device, or use` --out <dir>` and set` CACTUS_LIB_PATH` to the shared library and` CACTUS_NEEDLE_WEIGHTS` ,` CACTUS_WHISTLE_WEIGHTS` or` CACTUS_MIRAGE_WEIGHTS` to the corresponding` .cact` file.
3. Download the Python package and dependencies with` pip download cactus-compute` , then install with` pip install --no-index --find-links <dir> cactus-compute` . Set` HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` so missing files fail immediately.


A platform download holds binaries only.` cactus download linux-arm64 --model needle3 --out ./runtime` also places the model beside the engine. Native inference needs no network connection.


## Environments


` cactus.environments` ships six ready-made tool surfaces:` smart_home` ,` media_player` ,` productivity` ,` wearable` ,` kitchen_appliance` and` data_capture` . Each module exposes` TOOLS` ,` SYSTEM` , a lazily constructed` agent` , a frozen` TEST_CASES` suite of 32 cases and` run_tests(min_confidence=0.0)` ;` python -m cactus.environments.smart_home` runs one suite and exits 0 on pass.


```text
from   cactus.environments   import   smart_home


smart_home.agent.complete(  "dim the study lights to 30 percent"  )
smart_home.run_tests(  min_confidence  =  0.4  )
```


Adapt one by swapping the` Literal` values for your own and keeping the shapes: closed sets as enums, bounded numbers, verbatim copy for free text, five tools or fewer.


## CLI


Command What it does


` cactus generate-data --tools tools.json --num-samples 500 --output data.jsonl` Synthesise training rows through OpenRouter (` --augment data.jsonl` expands a set).


` cactus finetune data.jsonl --epochs 10 --out adapter.safetensors` LoRA on the frozen base;` --lora-rank` ,` --lora-alpha` ,` --lr` ,` --batch-size` ,` --max-len` ,` --val-split` ,` --seed` ,` --generate <n>` .


` cactus build --lora adapter.safetensors \[--layers N\] \[--platform <folder>\] \[--bits 2|4\] \[--upload\] --out <path>` Merge, slice, quantise, package the tokenizer; with` --platform` , also fetch that platform's engine and header.


` cactus fetch \[--platform-tag <tag>\] \[--out <dir>\]` Pre-download the engine wheel for this or another machine.


` cactus download needle3 | needle3.safetensors | <org>/<repo>\[/<file>.cact\] | <platform> \[--out <dir>\]` Pull the base archive, the checkpoint to fine-tune, a published archive, or a platform folder.


` cactus playground \[--weights my.cact\]` The browser UI locally at` http://127.0.0.1:7860` .


` cactus whistle playground \[clip.wav\] \[--language en\] \[--keywords "..."\] \[--word-timestamps\]` Speech to text in the terminal: Enter to record, Enter again to stop, or pass a WAV. Needs the` \[mic\]` extra to record.


` cactus whistle compare \[clip.wav\]` The same clip through Whistle, Whisper tiny, Whisper base and Moonshine tiny v2, with each one's timing. Needs the` \[mic,compare\]` extras.


` cactus whistle finetune train.jsonl validation.jsonl test.jsonl \[--tokens <file>\] \[--language <code>\] \[--epochs 3\] --out adapter.safetensors` LoRA on the frozen Whistle base, scored on the test set; a new language code adds that language,` --tokens` adds words or characters to the vocabulary.


` cactus whistle build --lora adapter.safetensors \[--layers N\] \[--platform <folder>\] \[--upload\] --out <path>` Merge, slice, quantise to 4 bits and package a tuned` whistle.cact` ; with` --platform` , also fetch that platform's engine and header.


` cactus download whistle \[--out <dir>\]` Pull the speech weights.


` cactus run --checkpoint <base> --query "..." --tools tools.json` JAX reference inference from a checkpoint, for development.


## Mistakes to avoid


- Expecting free-text answers. Unsupported input returns an empty call; handle it.
- Reading` arguments` keys that were not evidenced in the input. Optional fields may be absent.
- Creating one` Cactus` per turn. Reuse the instance so context carries; a new toolset is a new instance.
- Passing a` .safetensors` or` .pkl` to` weights=` . It expects a` .cact` from` cactus build` .
- Loading an archive exported by an older package. The` .cact` format is tied to the engine version; rebuild it.
- Assuming every custom archive has a calibrated confidence head. Archives without one return` confidence=None` ; validate their outputs yourself.
